newsitem.title: UK: UK devolution plans a con, Conservative Hague says.
newsitem.headline: UK devolution plans a con, Conservative Hague says.

text.p: William Hague, a leading contender for the job of Conservative party leader, said on Tuesday that the government's devolution plans were a con designed to appease those who want to break up the United Kingdom.

Setting out his stall on the eve of the Queen's speech detailing Labour's initial legislative programme, Hague said he would also oppose government plans to legislate for a minimum wage, a windfall tax on privatised utilities and abolition of the scheme that helps poor children attend private schools.

"We will be a constructive Opposition. We will attack Labour when they are wrong. We will improve their proposals when we can. And we will not be afraid to support their plans if they are right," he said in a statement.

Hague, the youthful former Welsh secretary, said government plans for pre-legislative referenda on devolution for Scotland and Wales were wrong because people would be asked to back the principle without knowing exactly what was on offer.

"The government is engaged in a deceitful exercise to con the people of Scotland and Wales into supporting far-reaching constitutional change before parliament has a chance to decide the details," he said.
Plans for a tax-raising parliament in Edinburgh and an assembly in Wales were nothing more than an attempt to appease those who wanted to break up Britain, he said.
"As with all attempts at appeasement it will ultimately end in surrender. We are determined to keep our United Kingdom together as one," he said.
